children: Pratt & Whitney has completed a design review of its planned F135 Engine Core Upgrade, advancing the program toward production for the F-35 fighter jet.

The risk reduction design review examined the upgrade’s detailed design, propulsion technologies, aircraft integration and testing preparations. It also assessed whether suppliers are prepared to support production and retrofits.

The upgrade is intended to provide the additional power and thermal-management capacity required for the F-35’s Block 4 modernization program. Block 4 calls for advanced sensors, weapons and other systems across all three variants of the aircraft.
For investors, the milestone reduces some of the technical and execution risk surrounding a program that could support long-term production and aftermarket revenue for RTX

. The ability to retrofit existing aircraft also expands the potential market beyond newly built F-35s, although future revenue will depend on government funding, testing results and the timing of production contracts.

Pratt & Whitney Military Engines President Jill Albertelli said in a statement that the review demonstrated the design’s maturity and moved the company closer to delivering an upgrade based on the existing F135 architecture. U.S. Navy Capt. Mitch Grant, the F-35 propulsion program manager, said the project remains on schedule to support the aircraft’s modernization.

Risk-reduction work funded under a contract awarded in 2024 includes design development, aircraft integration, test preparation, engineering and supply-chain readiness. Pratt & Whitney said the upgrade is designed to be installed in newly produced aircraft or retrofitted at F135 maintenance depots.

The company has delivered more than 1,500 F135 engines to customers across 20 allied countries. Pratt & Whitney plans to retain substantial commonality with the current engine as it develops the upgrade, potentially limiting changes to the F-35’s existing production and maintenance network.

title: RTX’s Pratt & Whitney advances F-35 engine upgrade toward production
